topics.tldr: This week's discussion highlights the growing inadequacy of traditional robots.txt for AI crawlers, with new proposals like ai.txt and llms.txt emerging for purpose-based content control, and a shift in crawler policy to a strategic, board-level concern for publishers navigating AI search visibility and monetization.

items.title: Search visibility now depends on being cited
items.frame: Crawler policy is now a board-level issue, affecting AI search visibility, training, and monetization, with Cloudflare offering pay-per-crawl options.
items.quote: The executive lesson is direct. Crawler policy is now a distribution decision. It belongs in legal, marketing, engineering, and leadership conversations.

items.title: GEO Audit on My Own Site: 59/100 — and Perplexity Already Cites Me
items.frame: A personal site audit reveals AI crawlers have full access, with Perplexity already citing content, suggesting blocking might be strategic self-harm for solo publishers.
items.quote: If you are a solo publisher, blocking is strategic self-harm.

items.title: Beyond Robots.txt: Implementing AI.txt and LLMs.txt for Purpose-Based Scraping Control
items.frame: Robots.txt is insufficient for AI scraping control; new standards like `ai.txt` and `llms.txt` are proposed for purpose-based content use and legal enforceability under the EU AI Act.
items.quote: Robots.txt falls short for AI crawlers because it is a voluntary, non-enforceable guideline in an increasingly hostile data environment where many AI agents simply ignore it.

topics.tldr: This week's key discussions on AI agents primarily focus on the evolving landscape of agent security, emphasizing new risks like prompt injection, over-privileged agents, and tool misuse in enterprise deployments, and the need for specialized security architectures beyond traditional controls.

items.title: Multi agent security: risks and how to secure AI agent systems
items.frame: Examines the fundamental shift in security for multi-agent AI systems, detailing new risks and the need for runtime defense and continuous visibility.
items.quote: Multi-agent security is not an extension of single-model security—it is a fundamentally different problem driven by autonomous systems that plan, delegate, and act across environments.

items.title: AI agent security: how to protect autonomous systems without slowing down the business
items.frame: Outlines the biggest AI agent security risks, including prompt injection and excessive permissions, and proposes controls for safe enterprise deployment.
items.quote: The moment an agent can read data, make decisions, and take action inside your business systems, your risk profile changes.

items.title: What Is AI Agent Security? Risks & Fixes In 2026
items.frame: Explores hidden threats and failures in agentic AI systems, arguing that traditional RBAC is insufficient and a data control layer is essential.
items.quote: Autonomous AI agents pull data from systems you secured, pass it between pipelines, write to memory, and act on instructions without a human reviewing each step.

items.title: Secure AI agents at scale using Microsoft Agent 365 | Microsoft Learn
items.frame: Discusses new security challenges introduced by AI agents at scale, such as agent sprawl and tool misuse, and how a distributed security model can address them.
items.quote: AI agents introduce new security challenges, including: Agent sprawl from user-created and SaaS agents that expands the attack surface.

topics.tldr: This week saw commentary on artists' role in addressing AI's copyright impacts and a UK government initiative to support smaller creative organizations in licensing their content for AI.

items.title: Artists can help us fight AI's existential threats
items.frame: This commentary argues artists are uniquely positioned to address AI's copyright theft and calls for regulation of AI training and updated copyright laws.
items.quote: Artists are disproportionately impacted by AI's tendency to steal work from creatives and deprive them of paid work – but artists are also uniquely qualified to explore the complex issues we now face.

items.title: Wednesday 29 April 2026 Daily Report of Written Answers and Written Statements
items.frame: A UK Parliament report details a government working group exploring support for independent and smaller creative organizations in licensing their content for AI.
items.quote: In particular, the 18th March 2026 Statement on Copyright and AI Progress announced a working group on independent and smaller creative organisations to explore whether there is a role for government to support their ability to license their content.

topics.tldr: This week's reporting highlights the ongoing tension between Google's growing search revenue, attributed to AI Overviews, and independent research indicating significant declines in publisher traffic and organic click-through rates, particularly impacting smaller media outlets.

items.title: Google Search Just Grew 19% With AI Overviews | NO-BS Marketplace Blog
items.frame: Google's Q1 2026 earnings show 19% Search revenue growth with AI Overviews, challenging predictions of revenue collapse despite potential publisher traffic shifts.
items.quote: Apparently, the user behavior changes that AI Overviews introduced did not produce the revenue collapse that critics predicted.

items.title: AI Overviews Clicks Get Tested, Earnings Tell Two Stories - SEO Pulse
items.frame: Google's Liz Reid defends AI Overviews by claiming they reduce 'bounce clicks,' but a field experiment shows a 38% drop in organic clicks.
items.quote: When AI Overviews appeared, organic clicks dropped 38%, and zero-clicks rose 33%.

items.title: Google on AI Overview Traffic Loss - Digital Marketing Desk
items.frame: Liz Reid reiterates that AI Overviews reduce 'bounce clicks,' but third-party data from Chartbeat and Pew Research indicates significant publisher traffic declines.
items.quote: global publisher traffic from Google Search declined by roughly one-third.

items.title: The Invisible Publisher | AIVO Perspectives
items.frame: AI platforms are consuming publisher content, leading to a one-third collapse in search traffic and an estimated $2 billion annual ad revenue loss, especially for smaller publishers.
items.quote: AI platforms are consuming publisher content, stripping away the brand, and returning almost nothing.

items.title: What Google & Microsoft Earnings Say About Search
items.frame: Google's Search revenue is growing, but this doesn't clarify outbound clicks to publishers, as third-party data shows significant CTR drops and traffic loss for publishers.
items.quote: Google's revenue can rise even as publisher traffic declines.
